title: WPSS/1011/2019 of PIYUSH KUMAR PANT Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
WPSS No. 1011 of 2019
Honíble Manoj K. Tiwari, J.
Mr. Navnish Negi, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Chief Standing
Counsel with Mr. Sushil Vashisht, Brief
Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. B.D. Kandpal, Advocate for
respondent no. 2.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Petitioner participated in a combined
selection for various non-gazetted posts held
by Uttarakhand Public Service Commission
and he scored 258.474 marks out of 400;
but, he was declared unsuccessful.
Respondent no. 3, namely, Mr. Arun Khulbe
scored 259.842 marks and he was
recommended for appointment as Supply
Officer.
According to the petitioner, there is
marginal difference of 1.4 marks between
him and Mr. Arun Khulbe. He submits that
there was variance in English version and
Hindi version of question no. 17, therefore,
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission
decided to allot bonus marks in respect of
the said question to all candidates, which
carried 10 marks. Petitioner is aggrieved by
grant of proportionate bonus marks of
question no. 17 to all candidates, according
to which, bonus marks to be given to a
candidate would depend on total marks
scored by him. This, according to the
petitioner, is unjust & illegal and the
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission
ought to have either granted equal bonus
marks or should have all together ignored
the said question by reducing marks from
200 to 190.

Per contra, learned counsel for
respondent no. 2 submits that decision
taken by Uttarakhand Public Service
Commission was applied across the board to
all candidates, therefore, no special
prejudice was caused to the petitioner. He
further submits that there is no allegation of
biased.
Learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that petitioner has already made a
representation ventilating his grievance to
Uttarakhand Public Service Commission on
07.04.2019, which is still pending
consideration. He, therefore, confines his
prayer and submits that the Competent
Authority may be directed to consider and
decide petitionerís representation and pass
appropriate order.
 Prayer made by the learned counsel
for the petitioner is innocuous, therefore,
deserves to be accepted.
Consequently, writ petition is disposed
of with a direction to the Competent
Authority in Uttarakhand Public Service
Commission to consider and decide the
representation of the petitioner dated
07.04.2019 (annexed as Annexure No. 8 to
the writ petition) by a reasoned and speaking
order, in accordance with law, within a
period of three weeks from the date of
production of a certified copy of this order.
 (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.)
Arpan 03.05.2019
